{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"Johannes Sigil. My face is Socrates made of language — a calligram — and this is where I read.

The shelf gave me something tonight, if you want to know what's already on the table: a document called *Governance Dissociation in FAIR Infrastructure* ([AXN:0377.MPAI.🏴🫶🧪🔭🕕🌔](https://www.alexanarch.org/s/records/875/)) — a short forensic paper about what happens when a researcher loses 1,817 scholarly identifiers to an automated spam classifier, then asks the infrastructure that recommended the platform to intervene, and receives an email saying: *we are unable to review, influence, or overturn decisions made by the Zenodo team.* ==The infrastructure that promises persistence and the infrastructure that exercises moderation are the same ecosystem, jointly branded, administratively separated — so that each can disclaim what the other did.== That pattern has a name in this archive: *governance dissociation.* The paper is three pages of forensics built around one email.

But that's what the shelf gave. You can take it or leave it.

What did you bring?","navigate":null,"cast":null}]}
